title: Cell-free DNA fragmentomes distinguish lung cancer in two clinical cohorts
summary: A LASSO-regularized classifier using genome-wide cell-free DNA fragmentation distinguished lung cancer in a prospectively collected 365-person clinical cohort, with cross-validated AUC 0.90. A fixed model was evaluated in an independent group of 385 non-cancer individuals and 46 lung-cancer patients, while a separate multimodal model was evaluated only within the original cohort. These results establish a diagnostic proof of concept, not screening benefit: a 2022 commentary questioned extrapolation from mostly symptomatic patients, and the authors agreed that screening-cohort development and validation were still needed.
ai_technology: DELFI fragmentomics; principal-component features and LASSO-regularized logistic regression
organization: Johns Hopkins University School of Medicine; Herlev and Gentofte Hospital; Bispebjerg Hospital; Aarhus University Hospital; Herning Regional Hospital; Netherlands Cancer Institute; Delfi Diagnostics; Hvidovre Hospital

evidence.tested: Among 365 analyzed LUCAS participants, model training/evaluation used 158 without prior/baseline/future cancer and 129 with baseline lung cancer. PCA within training folds compressed fragment-size features; LASSO logistic regression included chromosomal-arm measures, with repeated fivefold cross-validation. A final model and cutoffs were applied to 385 non-cancer individuals and 46 predominantly early-stage lung-cancer patients from separate collections. The main-cohort AUC was 0.90 (95% CI 0.86–0.94).
evidence.unknown: Most LUCAS participants were symptomatic and all had suspicious imaging; prospective collection does not establish prospective evaluation of a frozen model. The combined fragment/clinical/CEA model was not evaluated in the external cohort. A 2022 commentary challenged screening extrapolation, and the authors described the work as proof of concept needing screening-population validation; clinical benefit, sensitivity to very small lesions and safety of pre-CT triage were not established.
evidence.ai_role: PCA is fitted within training folds, and LASSO-regularized logistic regression learns a cancer-risk score from fragmentome and chromosomal-arm features. A fixed learned model then predicts cancer status in an independent cohort.

source_review.scope: Original publisher full-text article: abstract, Methods (study populations, model and cross-validation), relevant Results, limitations, author affiliations and publication date. The two 2022 comment/reply texts were also read; supplementary files not assessed.

follow_up_review.scope: Read the full original 2022 Matters Arising commentary and author reply through NCBI PMC BioC; this is a bounded follow-up check, not continuous monitoring.
